SUBJECT: POTENTIAL PROCESS MODIFICATIONS /599
In order to assist us im the development of new products, we need to
obtain an estimate of the impact that various process modifications
may have on the Macon plant. New process and product technology is
developing in several areas including the use of a CTO process, imple—
mentation of additives to tobacco, development of a longer lasting
cigarette, new blends and materials which are more brand specific,
etc. These projects span the entire range from new product develop-
ments to needed improvements on current brands. Our needs in these
areas are obviously immediate from an overall Corporate viewpoint.
However, we also recognize the realities of the impacts changes to our
process and materials will have in manufacturing.
What we need then is an ability to rationalize these objectives and
short-term constraints. In order to accomplish this rationalization,
we will need your input from the viewpoint of the degree of difficulty
of implementation.
More specifically, we necd estimates for cach of our considered modi-
fications addressing items such as cost, timing, degree of difficulty,
resource needs, etc. We can then utilize this data to both guide our
development efforts as well as reconcile any differences ia time
frames and priorities.
A list of some of the modifications we are currently considering is un
attached. Relative to the information we need, we are aot looking for wR
“to-the-penny" estimates. A quicker response is more important than a oe
fine-tuned estimate. At the same time, recognize that our programs =
will be impacted and a degree of accuracy is essential. we

as an analogous feeling as a pepper taste and differs froa
the strength feeling which is related to the nicotine
concentration. °

the nicotine and it is not included into a taste definition.
Fullness is defined as a total feeling in the mouth. Tobacco
aroma is a specific tebacco smell (skeletal tobacco has no
aroma).

From: Darienne L. Dennis
Subject: ANNUAL MEETING. UPDATE ON INFACT ACTIVITIES
Today was the official launch of INFACT’s national boycott of PM and RJR
Nabisco products. To date, the following has been reported:
* New York: Jim Wegman of PM’s Security Department met with six INFACT
representatives today outside of 120 Park.
Two individuals had first come into the lobby, asking to see Mr. Miles. Jim was
there, greeted them cordially and explained that (1) one can’t see Mr. Miles
without calling in advance for an appointment; (2) that the lobby was private
property and would they mind stepping outside. The conversation continued on
the sidewalk --all being captured by an accompanying photographer.
The group consisted of six people --three older men, two older women and a
young man. They all wore “Stop Joe Camel” buttons; the young man carried a
small banner, “Stop Addicting Children.” They al] passed out feaflets; copy
attached.
* San Francisco: A rally is scheduled today from 4:00 p,m, to 6:00 p,m, (pacific
standard time) at Children’s Park in Golden Gate Park. We will have more details
on this event later this evening
* Los Angeles: Reportedly, no rally is scheduled for Los Angeles today.
However, two groups will be distributing materials on the boycott. Three people.
from Peace & Justice will be handing out flyers in front of the Catholic Chancery
Office at West 9th Street in Los Angeles. One or two employees from Mrs.
Gooche’s (a health-food grocery store chain) will be distributing flyers at one of
the store locations in Coldwater Canyon/Studio City.
We are continuing to monitor the situation throughout the country, particularly
keeping a close watch for any activities during this evening’s rush hour. We will
update you on any new developments as we become aware of them

FROM: Bill Murray and Geoff Bible
We want to share with you the details of an exciting new advertising
campaign. This campaign is not about a product, it's a straight talking
approach to explaining our point of view on some of the issues surrounding
tobacco.
As we have traveled throughout the company and met with employees these
last few months, we have both been impressed by the pride people express
in what we do, and by the desire to speak up for what's right. And so, we
decided it was time to share more directly with the American people our
position on tobacco issues that are now being debated every day around the
country. Further, we want the American people to know the facts because
we hear from people time and time again that “facts matter.”
Therefore, starting today and continuing for the next several weeks, Philip
Morris will launch an advertising campaign entitled “Where We Stand.”
With straight-forward plain talking ads, the campaign will explore our
position on important tobacco Issues and the controversy surrounding them.
Attached to this mailing are copies of the ads that we will run over the next
three weeks.
| We want ali of our employees to understand our position on these issues, and
we encourage you to read these ads carefully so that you may be able to
discuss it with your colleagues and family members who may be confused or
even distressed by some of the accusations they read in the media.
In the weeks ahead you can look forward to regular “Where We Stand”
updates in our various company publications and mailings, inchiding the PM
Globe.
The “Where We Stand” informational campaign can help end some of the
hysteria around the country about the tobacco fssues. We want you to be a
part of this campaign and share this important information with others.
Feel free to send us your thoughts about other issues we may want to discuss
in future ads.

As you may be aware, today was the final day to submit comments to the Food

of comments, a majority of which opposed the FDA’s proposed regutations
Today in Washington, we at Philip Morris joined Tne Tobacco Institute and
other members of the tobacco industry ata news conference, during which we
made public our cornments to the FDA
Speaking on behalf of the industry, | restaied the industry's commitment to
preventing minors from having access to cigarettes. | also outlined the
numerous reasons why we believe the FOA's plan to regulate cigarettes is
illegal and excessive. “The FDA's proposal is not really about preventing youth
emoking. FDA seeks to ban commen promotional practices and impose
requirements that would interfere with adults’ choices and tne rights of cigarette
companias to sella legal product. A complete copy of my remarks from todays
news conference is attached
| would like to express senior management's heartfelt thanks to each of you who
took the time to contact the FDA on this most importantissue. A special thank
you to those who went the extra mile by asking friends, family members and

vendor. We also put a hold on all of the affected product that was within our
control.
Ongoing testing revealed that the presence of the bacteria triggered a
chain reaction which led to the formation ot a byproduct by the natne of methyl
isothiocyanate (MITC), a taxic substance. MITC can cause various forms of
discomfort, including eye, nose and throat irritation, dizziness, coughing, and
wheezing, if inhaled in sufficient quantities, .
We have no evidence that any of the affected product reached the retail
distribution channel. However, it is possible that some of it did, and we cannot
gasily or quickly verify that fact. Accordingly, because we are dealing with a toxic
substance, we decided out of an abundance of caution to institute a nationwide
consumer recall. As a result, we are recalling in the U.S. domestic market every
pack of cigarettes, both at retail and wholesale, of ail of the brands shown on the :
attached list. That recall was launched at 3.00 p.m. which is within one day of our 8

Project Review
Method development on gas phase analysis began with the purchase
of the Varian 3600 multiple detector gas chromatograph in November
of 1988. A 60 meter DBWAX column was initially used and evaluated
with injections of gas phase components. A eix port valve was
installed on the Varian GC in March of 1989 for introducing gas
phase smoke to the column via a sampling loop and a portable
smoking machine, With the installation of a liquid nitrogen valve
for oven cryogenic cooling a 30 meter DBS capillary column was
instailed (1). A splitter was connected at the end of the column
dividing the column effluent to both the FID and NPD detectors.
The output signal from the FID and NPD detectors was linked to the
Dec system using the Nelson software in September 1969. Various
columns and combination of column were tested to improve separa-
tion and resolution. In December of 1989 a 100 meter xX 0.25 mm X
0.5 pm was purchased form Supelco and installed initially on the
Finnigan 1050 GC/MS and used for gas phase component identifi-
cation. Early in 1990 the Petrocol column was installed on the
Varian 3600 (2). A Borgwaldt RM 1/G single port smoker was
purchased and installed in March of 1990. The fifth puff was
initially selected for analysis, later the puff selected was
modified to be the next puff after the burnline passed a point
35mm from the tipping paper.

At noon today the Senate passed, by voice vote, Senator Lautenberg’s "PRO-FEDS"
legislation as an amendment to the Treasury, Post Office and General Government
Appropriations Bill, H.R. 2403, The amendment would ban smoking in the Federal
workplace except in “separately ventilated” areas, The amendment is the same as S. 262
(enclosed) except for (1) the deletion of the provision establishing an Environmental
Tobacco Smoke Advisory Office at EPA (p. 12) and (2) the addition of an exemption for
VA hospitals.
Only Senators Ford and Lautenberg spoke on the Senate floor. Other Senators
submitted statements for the record. (The Congressional Record of the debate will be
forwarded as soon as it is available.) Senator Ford’s remarks focussed on the experience
of the airlines where air quality has declined over the years since the airline smoking ban
was enacted.
Immediately afterwards the Senate passed, by voice vote, a Bingaman Amendment
banning, in Federal buildings, the sale of tobacco products in vending machines and the
distribution of free samples of tobacco products, except in areas where minors are
prohibited. Bingaman’s amendment is essentially the same as his bill, S. 673 (enclosed)
introduced in March.
Last year Senator Lautenberg offered his “"PRO-KIDS" amendment to the Labor-HHS-
Education Bill, The Senate approved that amendment, by voice vote, September 16,
1992, but it was dropped during the conference due to the objections of Congressman
Natcher.
Efforts will be made when the conferees meet on H.R. 2403, most likely in September,
to delete or modify both the Lautenberg and Bingaman Amendments. @

Re: ACS "smoking or health" conference, cpening session
Conference chairman Charles LeNaistre opened the general session
by citing the 350,000 excess death figure. The conference, he told
the 250 invited participants, is an "opportunity to awaken America
by producing a national blueprint for action that is realistic and
achievable." :
He called upon the various work groups to produce a document that will
unite the 21 sponsoring agencies, while stressing that the conference
is not an ACS affair. Position papers forthcoming from the various
work groups will outline the ‘magnitude of the problem,” what has
been done in che past, “cebstacles" to solution, steps to solution, and
long range plenning.
Apart from a .S-minute keynote address by HHS Secretary Schweiker,
the rest of the morning session was devoted to an address by former
SG Luther Terry and a discussion of his address by a five-member
panel.
Schweiker's talk, politely received by the audience, was another
call for voluutarism. Schweiker, describing his advocacy of a
policy of prevention rather than cure, talked of a stepped-up HHS
campaign to educate the public as to how they can change their
habits to reduce health risks. He mentioned a new focus at HHS on
information d.ssemination, including a 10-year program at the Heart,
Lung and Blood Institute aimed at health education.
Also a major soal at HHS, he said, is a stepped-up employer-based well-
ness initiative campaign. Telling the audience "there are few health
dangers as serious as those caused by smoking, he promised to fight
for full fund ng for the Office on Smoking and Health in the 1985
budget.
terry, taking the 1964 Surgeon General's Report as a point of refer-
ence, devoted his 45 minutes to a discussion of what is known now
that wasn't known then, how well the 1964 report has stood the test
of time, and "is cigarette smoking less of a problem than it was
then?"
The validity of the 1964 report, which Terry described as "ane of
the most sign.ficant scientific reports in medical history," has
been strength:ned by time, he said.

Attached is a booklet containing a good deal of background
information on the convenience store industry including
material on the industry's major association, its largest

tobacco products. The booklet also describes efforts -- many

with the convenience store industry.

all field staff and others with issues responsibilities. We
will also begin implementation of all projects not already
